title: feat(scenarios): publish @objectstack/scenarios with an objectstack-scenarios CLI (npx), carrying the open cards only
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XQogyQWa7pC8SuBM9gesGp2)_

Fixes #31172

Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`@objectstack/scenarios` 去掉 `private`,随 `@objectstack/*` 发版列车一起发布,带一个命令 `objectstack-scenarios`。`npx @objectstack/scenarios run …` 就是今天的 `run-scenarios`,参数、默认值和拒绝规则完全相同;包里只带开放卡库(`docs/qa/scenarios/*.json` 与能力区清单),构建时拷进 `dist/library/`。
- 为什么改:维护者原话「把执行器发布成一个独立的命令行工具，同意」。外部团队和其他 agent 工具不用克隆平台仓库就能跑卡片。不是 `os` 子命令,裁决 D 不变。
- 风险与回滚:新增一个公开包和一个命令,已有包的行为不变;最大的风险是私有卡片随包外泄,所以打包测试对 tarball 做白名单:除了 `package.json`、与 `docs/qa/scenarios/` 逐字节相同的卡片、与能力区逐字节相同的清单,任何 JSON 出现都红。回滚即 revert 本 PR(发版前没有任何东西发布出去)。
- 先看:`packages/qa/scenarios/test/build/packed-tarball.test.ts`(打包白名单与命令冒烟)、`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/library.ts`(装在 npm 里时去哪读卡库)、`packages/qa/scenarios/scripts/pack-library.mjs`(只拷两个目录)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run test/build/packed-tarball.test.ts`,预期 10/10 通过(打包、解包、用纯 Node 跑 `objectstack-scenarios`,读到包内 9 张卡,`--packages workspace` 与 API key 登录都被拒)。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **The package is published** (`packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`): `private` removed, `publishConfig.access: public`, `files: ["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md"]`, `engines.node >=22`, all copied from the nearest published sibling (`@objectstack/verify`). It joins the changesets `fixed` group (`.changeset/config.json`), so it versions with the train; nothing is bumped by hand (it stays `0.1.0` in the tree until the release's `changeset version`). The description now says what it is: published, with the CLI and the open library.
- **The command line, a thin wrapper.** `bin.objectstack-scenarios` is `bin/objectstack-scenarios.js` (the `create-objectstack` pattern): it imports the BUILT `dist/bin.js` and nothing else. `src/bin.ts` (`runCli`) dispatches `run` to the runner CLI's own `main` with every following argument unchanged, plus `help` and `version`. The runner is imported lazily, for `run` only, and the build keeps it out of `dist/bin.js`: a tsup esbuild plugin (`binLoadsBuiltCli`) turns that import into one of a separate built entry, `dist/cli.js` (`.cjs` for the CJS build), so `help` and `version` load `dist/bin.js` alone (1.5 KB; measured 30 ms, against about 1.2 s warm for the runner's graph). `runner/cli.ts` is not restructured; it changes in two places: where it finds the repository (below), and one refusal (next bullet).
- **The open library as package data.** The build's new step `scripts/pack-library.mjs` copies `docs/qa/scenarios/*.json` and `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/*.json` (one level, regular files, nothing else) into `dist/library/`, keeping the repository's layout. The package's `turbo.json` adds both directories to the build's inputs, so a card edit invalidates the cached build the release would otherwise replay (`$TURBO_EXTENDS$` keeps the root inputs; measured with `turbo run build --dry=json`: 25 `docs/qa` inputs, 9 cards + 16 areas).
- **Where the runner reads the library** (`src/runner/library.ts`, `locateLibraryRoot`): in a checkout it is the repository, as before; installed from npm it is `dist/library/`. A checkout is recognised by the package sitting at `packages/qa/scenarios` of a pnpm workspace holding `docs/qa/scenarios` (compared by real path), so an install inside some other workspace is never read as one. `cli.ts` uses it instead of `findUp(pnpm-workspace.yaml)`, which from an npm install would have found the user's workspace or thrown. From npm, `--out` defaults to `./scenario-runs` (not into the package), and no framework commit is stamped (the package may sit in someone else's git repository). `libraryOf` is unchanged: the shipped copy is the `open` library, any `--cards` directory the overlay.
- **`--packages workspace` is refused from npm** (`cli.ts`, right after the library root is located): workspace mode (#31188) builds and packs a checkout's packages, and an installed package has none, so the run stops with that reason before it creates a work directory, builds or packs anything. `published` (the default) is unchanged.
- **README**: "Running from npm" (prerequisites, the cards it carries, where records go, the package source, not an `os` command); the intro and build paragraphs no longer say "private, unpublished".
- **Changeset** `.changeset/31172-publish-scenarios-cli.md`, `patch`, with both declaration lines. Corrected from `minor` in `9742af04`: with `Metadata-protocol: none` the launch-window level rule (ruling A on #25105) grades it `patch`, and `Check Changeset` refused `minor`.
- **`packages/spec/llms.txt`**: its package-ecosystem section counts the published packages and `check:llms-txt` re-derives the count from the workspace, so it moves 74 → 75. Not the expected surface; named here because the gate makes it this PR's. The file ships in `@objectstack/spec`, which is in the same `fixed` group, so it goes out with the next release either way.

### Public surface (Clause-②: yes), measured on the built entry declarations

Read with the TypeScript checker (`getExportsOfModule`) over `dist/*.d.ts` after a full build of this head:

| Subpath | Exports | Values | Type-only |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `@objectstack/scenarios` (`dist/index.d.ts`) | 79 | 55 | 24 |
| `@objectstack/scenarios/score` | 38 | 17 | 21 |
| `@objectstack/scenarios/score/full` | 56 | 25 | 31 |
| `@objectstack/scenarios/runner` | 165 | 118 | 47 |
| `@objectstack/scenarios/export` | 68 | 39 | 29 |

These five subpaths existed (private) and are unchanged by this PR except that they are now on npm (`./runner` and `./export` count what #31188 added to them on main). New: the `objectstack-scenarios` command (`run`, `help`, `version`). `dist/bin.js` (`runCli`, `USAGE`, `CliIo`) and `dist/cli.js` (the runner CLI) are not `exports` keys, so a consumer cannot resolve them; `library.ts` is not re-exported from `./runner`.

## Tests

- **`test/build/packed-tarball.test.ts`** (new, 10 cases): `pnpm pack` from the package directory (the tarball `pnpm publish` uploads), then the tarball extracted into a project of its own with each runtime dependency linked to the workspace build.
  - The manifest is public, names the bin, and has no `workspace:` range left.
  - Every card of `docs/qa/scenarios/` and every area of `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/` is in `dist/library/`, byte for byte.
  - **No other JSON anywhere in the tarball**: an allow-list of `package.json`, those cards and those areas. A card from anywhere else, wherever it lands, fails this case.
  - Every shipped card is `origin: generic`.
  - No TypeScript source (only `.d.ts`/`.d.cts`), and no `src/`, `test/` or `scripts/`.
  - `dist/bin.js` imports `fs`, `path` and `url` and nothing else statically, and reaches the runner only through `import("./cli.js")`.
  - The packed bin under plain Node: `--help` (exit 0), `version` (the packed version), no command (exit 2); `run --only no_such_card` loads the shipped library from `INSTALL/dist/library/docs/qa/scenarios` with no refusal and exits 2 with exactly that one line; `run --packages workspace` exits 1 on the refusal and creates no work directory; with a stand-in `claude` on a subscription login and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, `run --only service_desk` exits 1 on "`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set" and scaffolds nothing.
  - **Budgets.** The three `run` cases each spawn Node over the runner's whole graph once: about 1.1 to 1.5 s each here, 5.7 s and 6.5 s cold on a CI Test Core runner (run 42400730182, where vitest's 5 s default timed them out). Each gets an explicit 30 s (`RUN_SPAWN_BUDGET_MS`), as `built-consumer.test.ts` budgets its own spawn of that graph. The help/version case is three spawns of `dist/bin.js` alone (123 ms here) and keeps the default. The whole file reads 5.1 s here.
- **`test/runner/library.test.ts`** (new, 6 cases): `locateLibraryRoot` reads the checkout from the sources, the packed copy from an installed package, never another workspace that holds a `docs/qa/scenarios` and a `packages/qa/scenarios`, and refuses an installed package with no library; `runCli` prints usage, refuses no/unknown command with exit 2, and hands `run`'s arguments to the runner CLI unchanged (`--bogus`, `--modes nightly` refused by `parseArgs`). The file imports `src/runner/cli.ts` itself, so the lazy import's transform is paid in the file's import phase, not inside a case.

<details><summary>Ablations (each restored: blob == HEAD, git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

All through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor x1 → x0, replacement x0 → x1); 1 and 2 on commit `2d69cfb4`, 3 on `2eb91a69`, 4 on `149e988b`.

- **Ablation 1, the copy widened** (`pack-library.mjs` `DIRS` gains `docs/qa/platform-checklist`): the inner script rebuilt the package (`pack-library` ran, `dist/library/docs/qa/platform-checklist/` then held `areas` and `coverage.json`) and ran `packed-tarball.test.ts` → `1 failed | 7 passed`, the failure being "carries no other JSON: a card from anywhere but docs/qa/scenarios is refused". Restored, and the package rebuilt afterwards (`dist/library/docs/qa/platform-checklist/` holds `areas` only).
- **Ablation 2, the checkout test loosened** (`library.ts`: the real-path comparison of `packages/qa/scenarios` with the package replaced by an always-true `String("ABL2").length > 0`): `library.test.ts` → `1 failed | 5 passed`, the failure being "never reads another pnpm workspace holding a docs/qa/scenarios as the checkout". The suite imports `src/`, so no dist leg.
- **Ablation 3, the runner bundled back into the bin** (`tsup.config.ts`: `esbuildPlugins: [binLoadsBuiltCli].slice(0, 0)`): rebuilt, `dist/bin.js` then carried 19 static `@objectstack/*` imports (196 KB); `packed-tarball.test.ts` → `1 failed | 8 passed`, the failure being "keeps the runner out of the bin". Restored, rebuilt.
- **Ablation 4, the workspace refusal disarmed** (`cli.ts`: its condition ANDed with an always-false `String("ABL4").length < 0`): rebuilt, `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in `dist/cli.js` and `dist/cli.cjs`; `packed-tarball.test.ts -t 'refuses --packages workspace'` → `1 failed`, the run reaching workspace mode and dying on `fatal: not a git repository` instead of the reason. Restored, rebuilt, preflight `--absent`: marker absent from all 81 built files, tree clean.
- The API-billed refusal the smoke test pins is the runner's existing behaviour, which this diff does not change, so it is not ablated.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **The private overlay cannot reach the tarball by construction and is refused if it does.** The overlay (objectstack-ai/cloud#3603) lives outside this repository; `pack-library.mjs` copies two named directories of this repository, one level deep; and the packaging test refuses any JSON that is not byte-identical to an open card or area. It runs in Test Core on every PR and in the merge queue, so a leak is red before it can merge, rather than at publish. The triage audit's ⚠️ asked for a check in the publish job itself; this PR does not edit `release.yml` (the release pipeline is outside the claimed surface): the release publishes from a commit whose Test Core ran this test.
- **The bin is a wrapper, not a second CLI.** `run` passes its arguments through; `help` names the flags and points at the README instead of copying the flag table, so #31160's `--model` flags (and any later flag) appear in `run` without touching `bin.ts`.
- **Interaction with #31188 (`--packages`, merged as `86e9ef0a`).** Merged into this branch (no rebase), as the order's serial note asked. `published` (its default) works from npm unchanged; `workspace` is refused there (What changes). Its exporter rule (refusing `workspace` records) is in `./export` and needs nothing here. Its workspace mode packs every non-private `@objectstack/*` package, so it packs this one too (76).
- `dist/bin.js` has no top-level effect (it only exports `runCli`); `bin/objectstack-scenarios.js` is the published entry. `dist/cli.js` keeps `cli.ts`'s own self-run guard, which compares `argv[1]` with its module URL, so it never fires under the bin.
- `dist/bin.cjs` and `dist/cli.cjs` are emitted because the package's build emits both formats for every entry; nothing reads them.
- The `framework` record field reads `unknown` for a run from npm; the packages a run used are stated by #31188's `packages` field.
- Out of scope, untouched: customer-facing acceptance cards, an `os` subcommand (ruling D on #30291 stands), any release action.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (Only `llms.txt` prose in spec.)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes (scoped to the package; the repo-wide run is CI's).
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (`llms.txt` is hand-kept; nothing generated reads it.)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English (the 维护者速读 block is the lane's Chinese summary).
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
